thread.title: Apple Cleared by EU to Buy Shazam

author: Nina Lee
title: Apple Cleared by EU to Buy Shazam
text:
European Union regulators cleared Apple Inc.’s (NASDAQ: AAPL) acquisition of music identification app Shazam on Thursday in a boost for Apple’s Music and Siri segments. The decision comes after months of investigating whether the deal would give the iPhone maker an unfair advantage over rival streaming services.
Apple said in December that it had agreed to buy Shazam, prompting European regulators to scrutinize the proposed takeover as part of a broader effort to examine the value of data when evaluating mergers.
In the case of Apple’s deal for Shazam, regulators questioned whether the app held important information on Apple competitors. The focus on data transfer is a departure from typical antitrust enforcement, which tends to zero in on how a deal may affect customers in terms of a product’s cost.
“Data is key in the digital economy. We must therefore carefully review transactions which lead to the acquisition of important sets of data, including potentially commercially sensitive ones, to ensure they do not restrict competition,” EU competition commissioner Margrethe Vestager said in a statement. “After thoroughly analyzing Shazam’s user and music data, we found that their acquisition by Apple would not reduce competition in the digital music streaming market.”
Shazam identifies music with just a short sample of the audio, and is already utilized in Apple’s Siri virtual assistant. Completing the purchase and expanding the software is likely to help Apple compete with rival music service Spotify. One of Apple’s newer focuses is to increase revenue in its services segment, which includes digital offerings like iCloud storage, apps and TV shows and movies.
